findings: No blockers found; source-only review, no tools run and no tests executed.

Immutable identity enforced: pinned Zenodo URL, size 99,014,629,647 bytes and MD5 verified before atomic rename of train.7z.part to train.7z; oversize stream aborts early; short/corrupt downloads end FAILED with the partial preserved.

No extraction and no patient data reaches models: the child only downloads and hashes; the worker sees only reviewed cell sources, the fixed CPU-probe JSON, and a single-key status enum that the orchestrator re-validates; worker has no file tools (ToolSearch plus colab-worker MCP only).

Private capture: worker protocol/stderr/cells/status written 0o600 into a fresh private directory; orchestrator records only exception type names, never exception text or remote output; child script, console, and identity receipt stay in the private Drive audit directory.

CPU/Drive/disk gates (COLAB_RELEASE_TAG + no nvidia-smi, real /content/drive mount, free >= size + 10 GiB) are enforced inside the executed cell, so a misbehaving or out-of-order worker fails closed; all refusals are nondestructive ('xb' opens, exists/symlink refusal, no deletes), preserving the prior Drive copy and local partials.

Review binding complete for this change: reviewed() requires a successful Fable approval with matching scope, reviewed_commit, response SHA-256, claude-fable-5 assistant model, and per-file SHA-256 of all four changed files before dispatch; scientific pins unchanged and the patient adapter retains its separate review gate; no paid provisioning; bounded by --max-turns 20 and a 400-second timeout.

Advisory (non-blocking): binding covers only the four changed files, so imported colab_patient/colab_worker helpers rely on their own existing review pins; the four-hour child limit needs roughly 7 MB/s sustained from Zenodo or fails cleanly; a killed child can leave stale RUNNING (documented, with a warning against blind relaunch); worker model pinned via --model while actual_models is recorded but not enforced.
